research_question: What is the effect of probiotics, compared with no active treatment, placebo, or usual care, on self-reported improvement in constipation (proportion of participants reporting improvement)?
treatment_label: Probiotic supplementation (any strain, dose, or formulation)
control_label: No active treatment, placebo, or usual care
outcome_description: Self-reported improvement in constipation: the number of participants in each arm reporting improvement (e.g. patient-rated relief, global improvement, or 'treatment success') out of the total randomized per arm, pooled as a Risk Ratio.
positive_direction: A positive effect (RR greater than 1) means that a larger proportion of participants receiving probiotics reported improvement in their constipation compared with controls, i.e. probiotics favour improvement.
search_queries: probiotic supplementation bowel symptom improvement trial
Lactobacillus Bifidobacterium constipation placebo controlled effect
inclusion_criteria: Study examines probiotics (any strain, dose, or delivery form) in participants with constipation or at risk of constipation
Includes a comparison group receiving no active treatment, placebo, or usual care
Reports some quantitative outcome relating to constipation improvement or relief (e.g. number/proportion of participants improved, or data from which this can be derived)
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, editorial, opinion piece, commentary, or purely theoretical paper)
No comparison between a probiotic treatment condition and a control/placebo/usual-care condition
No quantitative outcome data usable for an effect size (no event counts/proportions, means+SDs, t/F statistics, or odds ratios)
Completely unrelated to probiotics and constipation (including studies of the assessment-based nursing intervention subgroup rather than probiotics)
moderators_to_extract: Probiotic strain or species composition (single vs multi-strain)
Control type (placebo vs no treatment vs usual care)
Population setting and age group (e.g. adults, elderly, children, hospitalized/institutionalized)
Risk of bias / study quality rating
effect_size_note: Pool as a Risk Ratio using each trial's reported number of participants with self-reported improvement in constipation and the total number randomized per arm. Restrict to the probiotics subgroup only; exclude the assessment-based nursing intervention subgroup.
